articles.title: Raúl Varela: "Nueve de cada diez madridistas quieren a Vinicius en el banquillo"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu analiza el cambio del brasileño, la irrupción de Diomande y apunta al desgaste de su renovación: "Algo se ha roto"
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu analiza el cambio del brasileño, la irrupción de Diomande y apunta al desgaste de su renovación: "Algo se ha roto"
articles.body: El momento de Vinicius en el Real Madrid ha cambiado. El brasileño atraviesa un inicio complicado y Raúl Varela, en La Tribu, analizó la situación de un futbolista al que ve diferente tanto dentro como fuera del terreno de juego. "Se ha abierto la veda. Vinicius ha caído en desgracia. Ya nadie quiere que baile en el Bernabéu", arrancó Varela. El periodista contrapuso la situación del brasileño con la irrupción de Yan Diomande, que se ha ganado rápidamente el cariño de la afición: "En apenas mes y medio Yan Diomande con un cuarto y mitad de regates y esas trenzas que tunea para cada partido se ha ganado el cariño de una afición que, como todas, está necesitada de caras nuevas y el costamarfileño entre otras cosas es precisamente eso, una cara nueva". Para Varela, la situación va más allá del rendimiento futbolístico. "Es una evidencia que Vinicius no solo está mal sino que está distinto y no me refiero a sus retoques físicos", explicó. El cambio también se aprecia, según Varela, en su comportamiento: "Por no ser igual que antes ya es que ni protesta, ni abre los brazos, ni hace aspavientos al colegiado de turno y por supuesto no rechista cuando es sustituido". Unas sustituciones que, según señaló, están siendo "bastante frecuentes en este arranque por parte de Mourinho", de quien añadió que "se dice que ya tuvo que leerle la cartilla por un desencuentro de entrenamiento". Varela también puso el foco en todo lo sucedido alrededor de su continuidad en el club. "La renovación, larga, sufrida, espinosa, con idas y venidas parece haberle pasado factura", afirmó. Para el periodista, "es como si lo hubiese desgastado y a la vez descomprimido" en su relación con Florentino. El diagnóstico de Varela fue claro: "Pero, como te contamos, algo se ha roto". Y puso sobre la mesa la situación de Mbappé para explicar el contexto que rodea actualmente a Vinicius: "Con la indulgencia que reina en Concha Espina en torno a la figura de Mbappé, más preocupado de su Balón de oro que de un título mayor, después de dos temporadas a Vinicius no le salen las cuentas". Además, Varela se refirió a las encuestas sobre la composición del ataque madridista. "Casi 9 de cada 10 madridistas le sitúan en el banquillo y conforman todo tipo de combinaciones en el frente de ataque", aseguró. "Kylian, Güler, Diomande, hay quien mete a Espí, quien adelanta a Bellingham. Cualquier trío calavera pero siempre sin Vini", añadió. Varela confía ahora en que el cambio de contexto con Brasil pueda ayudar al delantero a recuperar su mejor versión: "A ver si de la mano del Tío Carlo y con el cambio de aires brasileños se le pone mejor cara". Y cerró con un mensaje directo sobre el reto que tiene por delante Vinicius: "Próximamente en sus pantallas: toca remontar".

articles.title: Man Utd selling pieces of Old Trafford pitch for £125 each
articles.summary: Manchester United is selling pieces of its Old Trafford pitch for £125 each, an initiative announced the same day the club reported its overall debt remains more than £1bn.
articles.body:
Manchester United are selling pieces of their Old Trafford pitch for £125 each.

The initiative was announced the same day that the club reported that overall debt remains more than £1bn.

The first batch put on sale has already sold out.

While United recorded a record revenue of £677.6m and a £22.6m operating profit for 2025-26, they had a pre-tax loss of £43m.

The 13-time Premier League champions also confirmed £63.5m had been spent on buying land for the team's new stadium, which is expected to cost more than £2bn overall.

For the first time in 14 years, the Old Trafford pitch was dug up this summer and stripped back to its foundation.

Sections of the turf were preserved, with pieces measuring 7x7cm then being placed in glass cubes.

The cubes are presented inside a black case.

The club website says that the cubes make a "priceless memento of iconic games played at home and keeps the memories of matchdays alive".

articles.summary: Este jueves comienza una nueva edición de la competición
articles.body: Las grandes potencias europeas vuelven a la acción este jueves 24 de septiembre en una nueva jornada de la UEFA Nations League. Las principales selecciones del continente saltan al terreno de juego con la obligación de sumar de tres en tres para asegurar su billete hacia la 'Final Four' o, en su defecto, amarrar la permanencia o conseguir el ascenso en la élite tras un inicio de competición exigente. El gran plato fuerte de la fecha lo protagoniza el choque de trenes en el Grupo A, donde los gigantes del fútbol europeo miden sus fuerzas en un duelo de máxima tensión táctica. El partido más destacado será el Países Bajos-Alemania, emparejados en el Grupo A2. Ambas selecciones estrenan seleccionador, Xavi Hernández se hará carga de la 'Oranje', mientras que Klopp debutará en la 'Mannschaft'. Los dos combinados cayeron muy pronto en el pasado Mundial, en los dieciseisavos, en penaltis ante Marruecos y Paraguay, respectivamente. El otro duelo interesante será el Portugal-Gales, del Grupo A4. Tras la salida de Roberto Martínez, Jorge Jesus se hizo con el puesto de técnico luso, que seguirá contando con Cristiano Ronaldo. En Estados Unidos, cayeron en octavos ante España con un gol de Merino. Gales, que ni participó en la cita mundialista, buscará empezar con buen pie la fase de la Nations League. Será la reedición de las semifinales de la Eurocopa de 2016, que ganaron los portugueses. En este mismo grupo de Portugal y Gales, destaca el encuentro entre Noruega y Dinamarca. De forma paralela, la jornada internacional del jueves se completa con una atractiva batería de partidos amistosos entre selecciones de la CONMEBOL, la CONCACAF y la AFC. articles.title: Ruibal avanza, pero su regreso al grupo todavía tendrá que esperar
articles.standfirst: No es seguro que su vuelta al grupo se lleve a cabo durante esta fecha FIFA de selecciones
articles.summary: No es seguro que su vuelta al grupo se lleve a cabo durante esta fecha FIFA de selecciones
articles.body: Sin prisa, pero sin pausa. Más de cuatro meses después de pasar por el quirófano en Barcelona para resolver unos problemas en el menisco externo de su rodilla derecha que venía arrastrando desde varios meses atrás, Aitor Ruibal sigue dando pasos en su recuperación. Aunque su vuelta al césped para unirse a la dinámica de trabajo con el grupo todavía tendrá que esperar. En un primer momento se habló del mes de agosto, con el comienzo de Liga, como el posible escenario para el regreso del polivalente futbolista catalán al equipo. Pero tanto el jugador como el cuerpo técnico y los servicios médicos del club han preferido ir dando pasos firmes para evitar cualquier tipo de problema. Así, a día de hoy no es seguro que Ruibal vaya a regresar a los entrenamientos con sus compañeros durante estas semanas de fecha FIFA de selecciones. Así, a Aitor todavía le queda un poquito para estar listo para volver. No va a ser cuestión de días, por lo que el escenario más probable es en el tramo final del parón o justo después, una vez haya regresado la competición, en la que el Betis disputará cuatro partidos seguidos en La Cartuja, dos de Liga y dos de Champions. Habrá que esperar por tanto para ver de nuevo a Ruibal sobre el terreno de juego en competición oficial en una temporada en la que su rol debe ser importante. Sin sustituto claro para Antony, más allá de la posibilidad de dar la alternativa al canterano Morante, y compitiendo además por un puesto en el lateral derecho con Bellerín y Ortiz, Aitor confía en volver a ser un comodín para Pellegrini. Tras más de cuatro meses en el dique seco, desde el club le lanzan un mensaje de apoyo en este tramo final de su recuperación. "Cabeza alta, toro. Te estamos esperando", compartió ayer el Betis en sus redes sociales. Su regreso, un poquito más cerca... pero huyendo de la precipitación.

articles.title: Monarchy-aligned PAM leads in Morocco election provisional results
articles.summary: Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) took 97 out of 395 seats in parliament, as turnout falls to 38 percent.
articles.body:
Morocco’s monarchy-aligned Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) has won the most seats in parliamentary elections, according to provisional results.

PAM took 97 out of 395 seats in parliament, overtaking its senior coalition partner, the liberal National Rally of Independents (RNI), Interior Minister Abdelouafi Laftit announced on Thursday.

The RNI secured 66 seats and the Istiqlal Party took 65, according to the provisional results. The Justice and Development Party (PJD), a centrist Islamist party that won 13 seats in 2021, surged to 54.

Turnout fell to 38.02 percent from 50 percent in 2021, according to official data.

Under the 2011 constitution, King Mohammed VI appoints the prime minister from the largest party, putting PAM in line to lead the next government.

The vote was the first since deadly Gen Z-led protests last year, and the next government will face pressure to address everyday concerns, including jobs, wages and the cost of living.

It will also oversee billions of dollars in investment as Morocco prepares to cohost the 2030 World Cup.

Since no single party is expected to capture an absolute majority, the winner will need to build a coalition government. Portfolios are split among the political allies, but the palace traditionally keeps key posts such as defence and foreign affairs under royal control.

PAM leaders have ruled out another partnership with the RNI. The two parties have traded accusations over failed policies.

PAM campaigned on a $37bn platform promising 1 million new jobs, better wages and continued investment in healthcare and social protection.

One possible candidate for prime minister is PAM’s Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, who would become the Arab region’s second female head of government, after Tunisia’s Najla Bouden, if appointed.

Another potential candidate is Fouzi Lekjaa, the budget minister and head of the football federation, who joined PAM weeks before the vote.

articles.title: Virgil van Dijk: Liverpool captain slams Dutch reporter following claims he forced Ronald Koeman to change World Cup tactics
articles.summary: Virgil van Dijk claimed media in the Netherlands had said that he had 'ruined Dutch football' after allegedly telling Ronald Koeman to change formation during the World Cup; Koeman switched to a back five against Morocco, but would be eliminated on penalties
articles.body:
The Liverpool defender captained his country during the tournament, where they were knocked out by Morocco on penalties in the round of 32.

The 35-year-old has retained his captaincy under new boss Xavi, and was involved in a frosty confrontation with a journalist during a spiky press conference ahead of Netherlands' Nations League clash with Germany on Thursday.

"One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five. That is utter nonsense," Van Dijk told one reporter.

"The fact is we simply failed at the World Cup. Those are the hard facts. We didn't play a good World Cup. It's not about me. You perform together. You're a team. Your claim that I destroyed Dutch football after the World Cup - that sort of thing is completely baseless".

Koeman utilised a back four throughout the group stages of the World Cup, but switched formation for the game against Morocco which the Netherlands led thanks to Cody Gakpo.

However, a stoppage-time equaliser from Issa Diop sent the game to extra-time and eventually penalties which saw Koeman's side crash out.

"The plan is devised by the staff. Nonsense is being spread so that I look even worse. That happens far too often," Van Dijk said.

"I was told that it was my fault we played with five, that Ronald Koeman and I have destroyed Dutch football.

"The plan worked for 89 minutes, even though it was a bad match. We almost broke through. The idea that I destroyed Dutch football makes absolutely no sense. I didn't decide that."

"I'm super open," Van Dijk continued when asked why he was giving short answers during the press conference.

"Sometimes things need to be said, right? Otherwise you're just listening to all the whining. With most of the media, I have zero issues. Never have. When nonsense gets put out into the world, how else am I supposed to deal with that?"

With Xavi now at the helm, Van Dijk says he is motivated to continue with the Netherlands as they begin their Nations League campaign before next year's Euro 2028 qualifiers.

"I needed a holiday with my family and then an important meeting with the national coach. After 10 seconds it was already clear that I would continue," he added.

"What did he say? That I am Virgil van Dijk. It is about trust, appreciation, how important you are for the team. Physically there is - and was - no doubt but you also want to feel appreciation and pleasure."

articles.title: Villa: "España, al igual que en 2010, mostró al mundo cómo se gana un Mundial"
articles.standfirst: El campeón del mundo se sienta con MARCA antes de que la selección estrene la segunda estrella en su camiseta.
articles.summary: El campeón del mundo se sienta con MARCA antes de que la selección estrene la segunda estrella en su camiseta.
articles.body: David Villa (Tuilla, 3-12-1981) es historia del fútbol español. Nadie ha metido más goles que El Guaje con la camiseta de España (59). Pero no solo por esa cifra. Forma parte de la generación que lo cambió todo, la de los campeones del ciclo de oro entre 2008 y 2012. La cara se le ilumina cuando habla de la otra estrella, la de Nueva Jersey, la que le hizo vibrar en la grada. Y sus palabras se cargan de cariño y entusiasmo cuando en la charla con MARCA aparece el nombre de Ferran. PREGUNTA. ¿Qué piensa al ver la camiseta con las dos estrellas? RESPUESTA. Sobre todo alegría y mucha satisfacción por haber conseguido la segunda. No solo por haberla conseguido, sino por la forma en que se consiguió. Tuve la suerte de estar presente en varios partidos. La manera de demostrarle al mundo cómo se gana un campeonato del mundo quizá es la mayor similitud con 2010, porque en ese sentido fue algo parecido. Estamos felices como españoles, como futbolistas y como amantes del fútbol español. Por la historia de España, incluso podría decirse que dos son pocas. Pero es importante tener dos y seguimos aspirando a más. P. ¿Qué diferencia hay entre vivirlo en el campo como jugador y hacerlo desde la grada? R. Fuera tienes más nervios, por lo menos en mi caso. Yo jugando estaba bastante más tranquilo y confiado. En la grada también estaba confiado, sobre todo en la final, convencido de que podía ser. Pero el gol no llegaba y al final lo vives con más nervios. Más tranquilo en algunos aspectos, pero un poco más nervioso. P. ¿Qué pensaba cuando parecía que el partido se iba a los penaltis, con el Dibu encendido? R. Yo creo que por eso la reacción de todos fue de tanta alegría. Éramos conscientes de que en los penaltis teníamos un gran portero como Unai y grandes lanzadores, pero la historia reciente nos demostraba lo bien que había competido Argentina en las tandas. Había ganado la gran mayoría de las últimas tandas, tanto en Mundiales como en Copas América. Se hacía difícil y, por eso, no llegar a los penaltis fue algo muy bueno para nosotros. P. ¿Le sorprendió la calma con la que jugó España el Mundial? Al principio, ante Cabo Verde, hubo muchas dudas y Unai acababa de entrar en el equipo. R. La verdad es que tuve el privilegio de estar con ellos en el partido previo a Austria. Si estás fuera, viendo todos los nubarrones que se montan, te sorprende esa calma. Pero yo vi la tranquilidad que tenían en el vestuario y estar con ellos me dio una confianza enorme. Los vi muy tranquilos, muy convencidos, sabedores de que eran uno de los grandes favoritos y de que se estaban haciendo bien las cosas. Pensé que iba a ser complicado que alguien les ganara y, gracias a ellos, así fue. P. ¿Le recordó al ambiente que vivieron en Sudáfrica? R. Sí, el ambiente sí. Obviamente somos selecciones diferentes, pero el clima que respiré allí me recordó mucho a Sudáfrica. Es verdad que para nosotros era un poco más fácil porque habían pasado unos años y había menos conexión con el exterior. Ellos tenían mucha más conexión. Pero sí me recordó la tranquilidad, la confianza y el buen ambiente que se respiraba. Disfruté mucho de ese día de entrenamiento y de poder verlos allí porque me volví mucho más confiado a casa. P. Luis de la Fuente dio al equipo muchas tardes libres para desconectar. R. No lo sabía, pero sí es verdad que creo que Luis de la Fuente es uno de los grandes responsables, entre muchos otros, de que se hayan conseguido estas cosas. Se lo he dicho personalmente. Una de sus grandes virtudes es que conoce perfectamente a los jugadores y sabe qué necesita cada uno, no solo dentro del campo, sino también fuera de él, que es muy importante. A lo mejor, con esto de dar las tardes libres, era consciente de que era muy bueno para la plantilla. Esa es una de sus grandes cualidades. Además de ser un entrenador extraordinario, conoce a la persona, no solo al jugador. Siempre he dicho, incluso antes de conseguir la segunda estrella, que era, es y será el entrenador indicado para estar al frente de la selección. P. ¿Qué diferencias y similitudes encuentra entre Luis de la Fuente, Luis Aragonés y Vicente del Bosque? R. Quizá esas similitudes de las que acabo de hablar. Tanto Luis como Vicente las tenían. Conocían bien nuestras personalidades y sabían cuándo había que hacer una cosa u otra. Y hablo de aspectos fuera del campo. Dentro del campo los tres son extraordinarios por todo lo que han conseguido. Pero fuera también conocían muy bien esa faceta y tenían ese punto que ayudaba mucho a la plantilla. P. Del gol de Ferran hablamos todos. ¿Se dio cuenta de la que salvó Cubarsí? R. Sí, claro. No me di cuenta de lo que pasó hasta ver la repetición porque no era consciente de cómo había conseguido sacar esa pelota. Yo creía que era gol. Cuando ves la repetición aprecias todavía más la dificultad de la acción. No solo llegar a la pelota, sino sacarla desde dentro de la portería y evitar el gol en propia puerta. Era dificilísimo. Creo que Pau hizo un Mundial extraordinario. Iba a decir fuera de lo normal, pero viéndole jugar ya no parece nada fuera de lo normal porque lo hace siempre. Aquella acción fue la guinda a un grandísimo Mundial desde el primer minuto. P. Que marcara Ferran también tuvo algo de justicia por el esfuerzo, el trabajo y la insistencia. R. Me alegré mucho por él. En aquel momento pensábamos que, aunque se la hubieran metido ellos en propia puerta, lo habríamos celebrado igual. Pero me hizo especial ilusión que fuera él por todo lo que ha dicho. Le tengo un cariño especial. Lo conozco desde hace mucho tiempo. Hemos tenido trayectorias parecidas, aunque él salió del Valencia y yo del Sporting. Además, hemos pasado por clubes similares porque los dos hemos estado en Valencia y Barcelona. Cuando fui a verles le vi muy ilusionado, pese a que las cosas no le estaban saliendo. Estaba convencido de que iba a llegar su momento en el Mundial. Yo también se lo transmití y le dije que estuviera tranquilo porque estaba seguro de que iba a aparecer. Y apareció en el mejor momento, o en el momento en el que más lo necesitábamos todos los españoles. P. Y gol del 7 de España... R. ¡Gol del 7! Muy contento por él, sobre todo porque creo que se lo merecía. Es un gran chico por cómo trabaja. Se lo merecía igual que otros muchos jugadores. Enseñó una lección a todos los jóvenes que vienen detrás: nunca hay que bajar la cabeza, aunque lleguen las críticas o los malos momentos. No había conseguido marcar en ese Mundial y al final el trabajo siempre tiene recompensa. P. Siempre ha dicho que no le importaría que le quitaran el récord de goles. R. No. Alguien me lo va a quitar en algún momento. Esa pregunta me la han hecho muchas veces. Me gustaría conservarlo durante mucho tiempo, claro, pero es una cuestión natural. Alguien me lo quitará y, si puede ser alguien al que le tenga más cariño, mejor. Me pondré contento y seguiré estando orgulloso de ser entonces el segundo, que también es muy difícil. P. ¿Ve a esta selección capaz de repetir una época como la de 2008, 2010 y 2012? R. Sí, por supuesto que la veo capaz. Y no por una opinión personal, sino por cómo están haciendo las cosas y por lo que demuestran cada vez que juegan contra rivales importantes. Han sido superiores a equipos de máximo nivel. Evidentemente, el fútbol cambia muy rápido y una Eurocopa o un Mundial se decide por detalles. Puede pasar que en un momento concreto la balanza se incline hacia el otro lado. Pero los veo perfectamente capaces y, obviamente, son uno de los grandes favoritos para conseguirlo. P. ¿Es un alivio para los de 2010 que haya otro 26 campeones de mundo? R. Yo creo que es muy bueno para todos que no solo haya 23 campeones del mundo en la historia de nuestro fútbol. Cuantos más haya, mejor. Vemos selecciones como Italia, Argentina, Alemania o Brasil, que tienen muchísimos campeones del mundo. Creo que es una gran noticia para nuestro país. Ojalá en el próximo Mundial se sumen muchos más. No sé si serán otros 26, porque cada vez el grupo es más amplio, pero ojalá haya muchos más convocados que puedan convertirse en campeones. P. Si hablamos de Oyarzabal... R. Es un espectáculo. No solo por el Mundial que hizo, sino por todo lo que hace cada vez que está con la selección y también en su club, aunque quizá se valore menos. Creo que es un delantero que encaja perfectamente en la idea del seleccionador y en el fútbol que quiere la selección. Tiene gol, trabajo, capacidad de asistencia... La verdad es que hizo un Mundial extraordinario. Además, sigue teniendo una edad muy buena para estar en las próximas grandes citas. Y eso es lo positivo: que estamos muy bien cubiertos, no solo en la posición de delantero, sino en todas. P. Ahora vuelve la competición. A lo grande: Inglaterra en Wembley. R. Sí, porque Inglaterra siempre va a ser una de las favoritas, junto a Francia. Además jugará en casa y eso es importante. También tendrá una presión añadida y, por lo que nos toca, ojalá la note. Pero jugar con su gente siempre ayuda. Va a ser complicado. Estamos hablando de una Eurocopa y de Mundiales. No hay nada fácil. Es muy difícil, pero yo confío mucho en la selección. P. Y su delantero se llama Harry y se apellida Kane R. Es un fuera de serie. Dentro del área es letal, como pocos ha habido. Va bien de cabeza, con la derecha, con la izquierda. No es lento, ataca bien los espacios y además ayuda mucho cuando baja a recibir. Es un jugador total. Intentas encontrarle algún punto débil y es difícil hacerlo. Cuando eres Harry Kane tienes muy pocos defectos. Es un delantero de máximo nivel. P. Para terminar, el Balón de Oro para Villa es... R. Un español. No tengo un candidato concreto. Siempre he dicho lo mismo cuando me han preguntado por el Balón de Oro. Pero creo que, por lo que hizo España, más allá de ganar y por la forma en que ganó, sería una gran guinda que el Balón de Oro fuera para un futbolista español que estuvo entre los 26 campeones del mundo en Estados Unidos.

images.caption: David Villa, con los balones con los que España ha sido campeona del mundo. Jefferson Acevedo

articles.title: La renovación de Bellerín, una tarea 'inesperada' para Fajardo y el Betis
articles.standfirst: El contrato del lateral no finaliza en 2028 como se anunció en su día sino el próximo verano
articles.summary: El contrato del lateral no finaliza en 2028 como se anunció en su día sino el próximo verano
articles.body: Todo apuntaba a que en la lista de tareas pendientes de la Dirección Deportiva en los próximos meses había dos nombres: Marc Bartra, cuyo contrato expira el 30 de junio de 2027, y Diego Conde, cedido hasta final de curso. Pero lo cierto es que hay un tercer inesperado protagonista en cuya más que posible renovación tendrán que trabajar próximamente Manu Fajardo y su equipo con un horizonte cercano: Héctor Bellerín. El lateral catalán jugó cedido por el Arsenal en el Benito Villamarín la temporada 2021-22. El siguiente curso pasó por el Barcelona, primero, y por el Sporting de Portugal, después. Y el verano de 2023 completó su regreso al club verdiblanco. En ese momento, el Betis oficializó su fichaje por cinco temporadas, hasta el 30 de junio de 2028. Pero tal y como ha desvelado ABC de Sevilla y confirman fuentes oficiales del club, el acuerdo firmado finalmente fue sólo por cuatro años. Es decir, Bellerín está ya inmerso en su última temporada contractual con el club. Superada una importante lesión que le lastró hace un par de años, Héctor ha encontrado la continuidad necesaria para hacerse dueño del lateral derecho del equipo de Pellegrini. Además, en este tiempo se ha convertido no solo en uno de los referentes del vestuario, formando parte del grupo de capitanes, sino en uno de los futbolistas que más han conectado con la afición y que mejor se identifican con los valores verdiblancos y su apuesta verde y social. En el Betis están muy satisfechos con el rendimiento que está ofreciendo Bellerín sobre el césped, con su ascendencia en el grupo y con la manera en que se vuelca con todas y cada una de las acciones que le propone la entidad. Del mismo modo, Héctor ha encontrado su sitio en el Betis y en la ciudad de Sevilla, donde está perfectamente integrado. Por lo que, si no ocurre nada extraño y aunque aún no han comenzado los contactos formales con su agente, esta unión debe prolongarse más allá del próximo verano, cuando finaliza el actual contrato entre ambas partes. Esta temporada, con Ruibal lesionado, Bellerín es uno de los jugadores que ha participado en todos los partidos oficiales del equipo de Pellegrini, siete de Liga y uno de Champions. Ha sido titular en seis de ellos, superando ya los 600 minutos sobre el césped, y a los 31 años de edad está viviendo una segunda 'juventud', ofreciendo un nivel de juego muy alto. Un fútbol que, salvo sorpresa, seguirá brillando en La Cartuja... con el sueño de llegar también a la vuelta a casa, al Villamarín.

articles.title: Álvaro Negredo: "Me encantaría entrenar al Sevilla"
articles.standfirst: El ex delantero nervionense forma parte del actual cuerpo técnico del Sevilla Atlético
articles.summary: El ex delantero nervionense forma parte del actual cuerpo técnico del Sevilla Atlético
articles.body: Álvaro Negredo dejó su legado en Nervión como jugador y hoy en día forma parte del actual cuerpo técnico del Sevilla Atlético. El ex delantero blanquirrojo sigue formándose en los banquillos y sueña con hacerse cargo en algún momento del vestuario del primer equipo, como ha confesado en una entrevista concedida a Flashscore. Ya formó parte del staff del División de Honor del club el pasado curso y este verano llegó al filial. "No sé dónde acabaré. Por supuesto que me encantaría entrenar al Sevilla, y a todos esos otros equipos también. También me encantaría probar suerte como entrenador en el extranjero. No cierro ninguna puerta. Como jugador, no tuve ningún problema en marcharme al extranjero, y como entrenador tampoco lo tengo", comentó. El vallecano se extendió hablando de cómo vive su actual etapa en el Sevilla Atlético. "Hay que asegurarse de que, cuando un jugador joven vuelva el lunes después de un partido, aunque las cosas no hayan salido bien, no pierda la motivación. Tiene que volver mentalmente preparado para demostrarte que te equivocabas. Muchas veces, un jugador pensará que es el entrenador quien se equivoca, no él. Tienes que hacerle entender que tiene que esforzarse más y seguir mejorando. También hay situaciones prácticas que se dan en todos los equipos. A veces, diez minutos antes del entrenamiento, se convoca a tres o cuatro jugadores para que entrenen con el primer equipo. Has preparado una sesión de entrenamiento y, de repente, tienes que cambiarlo todo y adaptarlo al número de jugadores con los que cuentas", comenzaba. Y continuaba: "Para mí, vivir eso me está enseñando a tomar decisiones más rápido, así que me lo estoy tomando como un año de aprendizaje. Lo estoy disfrutando; intento ayudar y aportar mi granito de arena, junto con Diego, Juanma y el resto del cuerpo técnico. Quiero aportar mi experiencia y dar mi punto de vista sobre situaciones que quizá ya haya vivido como jugador. Me lo tomo como una etapa de aprendizaje, pero también como una oportunidad para aprender a tomar decisiones rápidas, a ayudar al equipo y a desenvolverme en un entorno que es casi semiprofesional, pero que está a solo un paso del primer equipo de un gran club como el Sevilla". Negredo también de la "conexión especialmente buena" que tuvo en el césped con Jesús Navas. "Estuvimos juntos cuatro años en el Sevilla y luego otro año en el Manchester City, así que cinco años en total. Rakitic era otro jugador que siempre buscaba al delantero con sus pases. Pero también tenía una conexión muy especial con José Antonio Reyes. Era un jugador completamente diferente cuando estaba en el campo. Sabía que, cuando recibía el balón, tenía que correr, porque sabía que iba a buscar ese pase hacia delante. También era un futbolista con el que tenía un vínculo emocional muy fuerte, porque nos entendíamos muy bien y me dio mucho apoyo, sobre todo durante nuestra etapa juntos en el Sevilla". El ex jugador lanzó una fuerte crítica a Peter Lim, el máximo accionista del club. "Al final, creo que cuando compras un club, cuando eres el presidente o el propietario, tienes que estar encima del club y realmente implicado en él. En los dos años que estuve en el Valencia, creo que vi a Peter Lim una o dos veces. Apenas lo vi durante esos dos años. Al final, daba un poco la sensación de que se trataba de comprar un juguete: "Me aburro, compro un juguete, lo dejo aquí, se lo dejo a mi hijo y que lo gestione otro"", señaló. "Si compras algo a esa escala, algo que implica a tanta gente y a tantos aficionados, tienes que estar mucho más presente. Tienes que dar la cara, sobre todo cuando las cosas van mal, porque el fútbol conmueve a muchísima gente, para bien o para mal", añadía. "Y cuando las cosas van mal, se nota aún más. Un club como el Valencia, con su historia, sus títulos y sus finales europeas, no puede ser abandonado por quienes lo dirigen. Algo tiene que cambiar. Hay que intentar darle la vuelta a la situación. Espero que, de alguna manera, el Valencia pueda salir de esa situación", añadía el actual segundo entrenador del Sevilla Atlético.

articles.title: Scotland: Robbie Ure delighted 'unusual route' from Rangers to Sevilla has earned first call-up aged 22
articles.summary: Robbie Ure is one of six newcomers in Sebastien Pocognoli's first squad; the new head coach takes charge against Slovenia in the Nations League on Saturday; Scotland are also away to North Macedonia with games against Switzerland and Slovenia at Hampden during this international break
articles.body:
The 22-year-old striker came through the Rangers academy before a lack of first-team opportunities meant a move to Anderlecht in 2023.

A spell at Swedish club IK Sirius followed, where 31 goals in 50 games made him a target for clubs across Europe in the summer.

He signed for LaLiga side Sevilla for an initial fee of £5.5m last month, and his rapid rise has been rewarded with a first senior call-up to the Scotland national team.

"At Rangers I didn't believe I could go further and I needed a step before the step and Anderlecht was able to give me that," he told Sky Sports News.

"Looking back now, it's clear that it was the right decision to make.

"It's a bit unusual for a Scottish player to take that route.

"A lot of people think it's only happened in the last four weeks, but for me it's been three years of working hard and moving to different countries and trying to get that opportunity.

"It's been quite long but it's been enjoyable.

"I did think there would be opportunities with the new gaffer. I'm happy to be involved in his first camp and hopefully I can show him what I can do."

It is a new-look Scotland under Pocognoli, with 12 players who were in Steve Clarke's final squad for the World Cup missing out.

None of the strikers who went to America are included in this squad, and Ure is hoping to take his chance.

"We need to bring a fresh energy, hard work as well and try and play how the new gaffer wants us to play," he added.

"For the strikers, the obvious one is we want to score goals.

"But there's more than that, and we're trying to get as much information and time on the pitch as we can to really implement how the new gaffer wants us to play."

The Pocognoli era officially gets under way in Ljubljana on Saturday, with a game against Switzerland at Hampden Park three days later.

The squad then fly to North Macedonia on October 3 before returning to Glasgow to face Slovenia again on October 6.

Scotland were demoted from Nations League A after a play-off defeat by Greece last year and return to the second tier for this year's competition.

"He wants us to play smart football, identify where the spaces are and be close together as well and a lot more things.

"It's early, and I think as this week and next week go by you'll probably be able to see a little bit more of what he's trying to get across."

articles.summary: Líderes en distintos proyectos deportivos comparten la base de trabajo de Emen4sport
articles.body: Edeporte de élite hace tiempo que dejó de depender exclusivamente del talento natural para apoyarse de lleno en el rigor científico y el control de la salud. Bajo esta premisa, la Torre BAT ha acogido este miércoles la jornada 'El Camino del éxito: Ciencia, Deporte y Salud', un encuentro organizado por Emen4sport y la UPV/EHU. La cita ha reunido a destacadas personalidades del sector para demostrar cómo la innovación tecnológica y el conocimiento académico son herramientas determinantes para impulsar proyectos deportivos del más alto nivel. A través de tres casos prácticos, los líderes de estos proyectos desgranaron el impacto real de esta preparación integral. Julen Guerrero, Mánager General del CD Estepona, puso en valor la ayuda de la empresa vasca en la histórica permanencia lograda en 2ª RFEF tras levantar 14 puntos de desventaja. Una visión estratégica compartida por Borja Junco tras el reciente éxito europeo del Bilbao Basket, y por Fran Contador, quien aseguró que el cuidado al detalle de la salud del deportista es el factor que explica el gran papel del Team Polti Visit Malta en el pasado Giro de Italia. El contrapunto desde la experiencia en el terreno de juego lo aportó el exfutbolista Raúl García, actual embajador de Emen4sport. El navarro subrayó que en un contexto donde la tecnología avanza sin descanso, ir de la mano de estos especialistas es "clave" para cualquier atleta que busque la mejora continua. El evento sirvió además para reivindicar la conexión directa entre las aulas y el deporte profesional, un puente que Unai Arzubiaga, vicedecano de la UPV/EHU, valoró con orgullo al ver cómo el conocimiento generado en la universidad rinde frutos en la máxima exigencia deportiva.

articles.title: Manchester City transfer news: Squad overhaul from a 650,000-strong database
articles.summary: BBC Sport goes inside Manchester City's data team, who have been a key part of their rebuild over the past 18 months.
articles.body:
Inside the confines of Manchester City 's sophisticated data operation is a fundamental phrase its experts work towards: "What does it take to win?"

In practice, the motto is broken down into three sections: identifying players, evaluating them and assessing how the club could improve them, all with a view to enhancing the statistical probability of City winning the Premier League.

Last season, the club's data department projected they would be there or thereabouts when it came to the title race, but their metrics indicated Arsenal were favourites to be champions. They were accurate.

This time around, City prefer to keep their projections under wraps - but five wins from five Premier League games have prompted predictions from supporters and pundits they will again be the Gunners' closest challengers.

City's devotion to data is at the heart of their efforts to close the gap on Arsenal and BBC Sport has been given unprecedent access to the inner workings of the club's metrics machine as we uncover some of the secrets guiding their work - particularly regarding player recruitment and sales.

Their work is a sign of the times in the Premier League, with clubs across the top flight and beyond increasingly using data for transfers and monitoring their teams' performance.

At City, one of the fundamental aims is to reduce risk of any market transaction, be it a purchase or a sale.

The system they play in at their current club and how the manager is asking him and the team to play.

Once those four aspects are observed, City's aim is to understand not just how good the player is but how good he could become at the Etihad.

Since winning the Treble in 2023 , City's squad has undergone a vast overhaul using this approach. Only four players from that historic campaign remain.

It is crucial to stress, however, that while data has made an indefinite impact on how City operate in the transfer market, the work of traditional scouts continues to be the primary gauge of whether they decide to move for a player.

"Data plays a role in our decision-making, but it is just one part of the overall picture," City sporting director Hugo Viana told BBC Sport.

"We know data cannot tell us everything about a player. It cannot fully show a person's character, mentality or behaviour.

"That is why we study data insights but focus on the expertise of our scouts and other specialists."

The prominence of data, however, has grown significantly behind the scenes at the Etihad.

Here BBC Sport can take you to the core of some of City's key transfer calls from their extensive three-year squad revamp - including the £116m signing of Elliot Anderson.

The starting point for any new signing is City's database of 650,000 footballers from around the world.

The next step is the brief: what sort of player is the club wanting to recruit.

This usually starts with a position, though that process isn't as simple as it sounds.

City, for example, categorise their full-backs into three types: those who are defensive, those who come inside, and those who play high and wide.

Once the club's data departments have the brief, filters that grade a player's overall ability are applied to whittle down the 650,000-man database to 20-50 names.

Juventus full-back Andrea Cambiaso is one player who has been on City's radar after the data highlighted him, particularly his ability to coming inside to build play in midfield.

That he is comfortable with both feet rated highly on the data, too.

In accordance with the data and the scouting reports it was decided the club would not proceed with their interest in Cambiaso in the previous window, but City's approach is likely to mean he will continue to be monitored.

The longlist of 20-50 names is cross-referenced with the scouting longlist. Generally there is a significant overlap between the players identified by data and the ones already on scouts' radar.

From there, further, more refined metrics are applied to rank and prioritise the longlist.

Scouts will then complete further diligence on the players to reduce the list to a maximum of about six players.

At this point, the club will complete deeper dives into the remaining players, including diligence on their injury record, athletic performance and behavioural habits.

The information is then collated into individual reports called acquisition packs which contain all the key metrics used to inform the decision on a player.

This includes a 'radar chart', which rates a range of specific on-field metrics.

For example, when Jeremy Doku was signed in 2023 , then manager Pep Guardiola decided he wanted a winger who was direct, akin to Leroy Sane, because at the time they had Jack Grealish and Riyad Mahrez, who preferred to keep the ball and cut inside.

Among the criteria applied in City's brief were the following: making (running into) the box, pressure regains, take-on percentage and opposition-half pressure.

Doku's overall numbers ticked the boxes Guardiola was looking for, although the Belgian's 'making the box' score was among his lowest readings.

Since his arrival, Doku has improved this rating - an example City say shows how their data systems are helping to improve existing players.

There is also a 'utilisation chart' that records how often the player has been used over a three-year period, as well as a scouting grade that indicates how highly the traditional scouts rate the individual.

Each player is also awarded an overall "current impact score" - which predicts what impression he would be expected to make immediately on signing - and a "potential impact score" that projects the contribution the player could make in the future.

Perhaps the most intriguing reading on the acquisition packs is a player's "action value score". This positions them in a league table that includes City players and ones from rival clubs who play in a similar role.

Once the acquisition reports are evaluated, the list is further reduced to 2-3 players once City's valuation of the player has been factored in.

Data contributes heavily to the price range City believe a player falls in, and the valuation is never a single number.

A decision is then made on which player is the priority, though all players on the shortlist are worked on simultaneously in the event of changing circumstances, for example if a player becomes unavailable.

Indeed, being able to move according to the market is something the data team feel they have become adept at.

The sudden emergence of Yan Diomande last season led to City completing checks on him before he joined Real Madrid from RB Leipzig.

The club also paid close attention to Eduardo Camavinga's metrics in case Real decided to sell a midfielder.

Anderson - the signing that shows City's forensic approach

Anderson was an obvious signing for a top Premier League club.

The 23-year-old had developed into a key player for Nottingham Forest . An added appeal was the fact he is English, and had cemented his position in the national team.

City fought off other top clubs, including Manchester United , to sign him .

It would seem, on the face of it, a straightforward decision.

But the way City analysed it underlines their incredibly forensic approach even when, outwardly, it might be considered they did not need to be so comprehensive given Anderson's obvious talents.

The fact they still used their algorithm and went through all their normal steps says a lot about elite football in the modern day - and also the limitations of data alone.

That is because - perhaps surprisingly - Anderson's metrics didn't necessarily catch the eye.

At the start of last season, despite emerging uncertainty over Guardiola's future, the club knew they would be in the market for at least one central midfielder come the summer.

They knew Bernardo Silva was leaving while there were doubts over the futures of Rodri and Nico Gonzalez.

There was an acknowledgement that replacing Silva and Rodri like-for-like would be virtually impossible, so they looked for a player who was equally adept at building play from either deep or high central midfield.

As last season developed, doubt also emerged over the future of Tijjani Reijnders - but Enzo Fernandez was viewed as the favoured replacement for the Dutchman.

Anderson made the initial cut from the 650,000-man database to the longlist - but was not high in that group. However, his metric readings didn't immediately scream out the "no-brainer" he ultimately became.

As City took a closer look, there was an acknowledgement Anderson's case does highlight some of the limitations of data.

Anderson did not score lots of goals for Forest, or consistently provide assists. Because, generally speaking, Forest aren't a possession team like City, his general metrics in their algorithm did not grab the attention.

With that in mind, City's data analysts had to consider that, because Anderson was generally playing closer to his own goal than he would at City, he wasn't getting the opportunities to impress in the final third of the pitch.

So they paid close attention to what he was doing at Forest and modelled his potential role in a City team that generally plays closer to the opposition's goal, dominates possession and has more elite players.

Among the criteria graded on Anderson's 'radar chart' were defensive regains, duel success, line-breaking passes, aerial-duel success and defensive errors.

With his reading for defensive errors, it was acknowledged that, because Forest were a transitional side, some were a result of the area of the pitch in which he was asked to operate.

He may, for example, have regained possession deep inside his own half but lost the ball because he had to play a longer and a riskier pass after being asked to play forward quickly.

In the same scenario at City, it is anticipated Anderson would have options to play a shorter pass with a greater success rate.

"Just because a player doesn't have the opportunity to perform a particular action on a regular basis because of the team he is playing doesn't mean he can't do it," said a source.

Anderson's data readings improved significantly as the season developed, which compelled the club's scouts to watch him on a regular basis.

He stood up very favourably against City's existing midfielders - and a list of rival players the club had identified as possible signings in that area.

The results of the diligence completed by City's data team, scouts and other experts meant that even though Anderson's price increased beyond what City believed was his true valuation, they felt the risk was low.

"Elliot Anderson is a great example of how the process works," Viana said.

"The data was positive for Elliot and gave us real confidence in his profile, but it was the insight from our scouts and wider performance team that helped us understand the player and his attributes and this proved our belief that he was the right fit for the club."

BBC Sport was also provided with fascinating insight into how data was used to sign Julian Alvarez from River Plate for £14m in 2022 .

The initial recommendation came from scouts, and given Alvarez was not a player originally identified by his metrics, the data team had to take a closer look.

Because the Argentine league isn't recognised as one of the strongest globally, City's general data settings mean players will reach a natural ceiling with their readings in comparison to those playing in one of Europe's top five divisions.

So, City dug deeper into Alvarez's stats, and his impact on both the ball and River's scorelines.

The stats showed he was by far the best player in the Argentine top flight, and City believed they had enough evidence to say he would develop into a starter for a top-half club in one of Europe's top five leagues within two-and-half years.

The data model valued Alvarez between £26m and £40m. City signed him for £14m so believed they were signing an undervalued player.

Alvarez's projected value was £70m after three years. They eventually sold him to Atletico Madrid in 2024 for £81m.

The signing of Abdukodir Khusanov from Lens also provides intriguing insight into City's reliance on data.

The 22-year-old didn't initially make City's 50-man longlist, but on closer inspection they found while his output on the ball needed to improve, his physical data - for example his covering runs behind - was through the roof.

Khusanov's on-the-ball metrics, City say, have improved significantly since he signed in January 2025.

The departure of Guardiola and the arrival of Enzo Maresca is not expected to alter the club's approach significantly.

The key metrics Maresca looks for in a player are understood to be very similar to Guardiola's, with the notable difference that the Italian prefers his full-backs to be more direct.

Rooted in City's coach recruitment process is a certain team philosophy and way of playing, with any new manager expected to produce a side that is possession dominant, can press high, regain possession high up the pitch, produce quality chances and entertain.

That philosophy was designed before Guardiola's appointment, and the Spaniard produced the purest form of City's footballing ideology.

With that in mind, the change in manager has not drastically altered the way City's data department approach their work.

Maresca will continue to work closely with them as he looks to build his own dynasty - but much of the hard work in building a squad to last is complete.

Before City's Treble-winning season, the internal data indicators were such that the club knew they would soon need to overhaul a squad that had reached its peak.

Selling players such as Kevin de Bruyne, Kyle Walker, Riyad Mahrez and Ilkay Gundogan wasn't easy given their illustrious service and the fact they were still performing at a very high level.

Data, though, allows the club to spot declining trends well in advance - often two or three years - before a player is offloaded.

Those particular metrics help City identify when the right time is to sell a player is - perhaps even before the buying club have spotted a drop in performance.

And when those trends are identified, the club can plan well in advance.

From there the club decide whether to start embedding a player from the academy or enter the market to replace.

Ayyoub Bouaddi's arrival from Lille this summer is a prime example. At 18, City realise he isn't necessarily going to have a profound impact this season - but the club believe the Moroccan will be able to make a bigger contribution within two years.

After the Treble season, the recruitment remit at City was to lower the average age of the squad and build a set of players that could deliver sustained success.

But doing that at City comes with a catch. Because at City, the team are always expected to compete for trophies.

Lowering the age of a squad is one thing; doing so while continuing to win is far more complicated.

In previous years, for example, City's data systems identified former Brighton trio Moises Caicedo, Marc Cucurella and Carlos Baleba, who have been lauded as data successes.

But there was a sense at City that the development of such signings would take too long for them to make an impact on a team that has the remit of winning titles or assets that could be developed and sold for a profit.

City have successfully lowered the average age of the squad to the extent they now have the third youngest set of players in the Premier League behind Newcastle and Chelsea .

But with the signings of goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, defender Marc Guehi, and Fernandez and Anderson they have added players who can not only grow with that new generation but also already have vast experience of top-level football.

City's data indicates their current squad will not peak for another two to three years - but also projects they are likely be among the title challengers this season.

articles.summary: El mejor duelo de este jueves, que tendrá como aliciente el debut de Xavi Hernández y de Klopp en los banquillos
articles.body: El estreno de la quinta edición de la UEFA Nations League nos regala este jueves 24 de septiembre uno de los choques más apasionantes y con mayor solera del panorama futbolístico internacional. Las selecciones de Países Bajos y Alemania miden sus fuerzas en el Johan Cruyff Arena de Ámsterdam en el duelo estelar de la primera jornada de la Liga A. Emparejados en el Grupo A2, ambas selecciones estrenan seleccionador, Xavi Hernández se hará carga de la 'Oranje', mientras que Klopp debutará en la 'Mannschaft'. Ambos gigantes continentales saltan al césped con el objetivo prioritario de sumar los tres primeros puntos. Sobre todo, después del mal verano que tuvieron. Los dos combinados cayeron muy pronto en el pasado Mundial, en los dieciseisavos, en penaltis ante Marruecos y Paraguay, respectivamente. El partido correspondiente a la jornada 1 de la Nations League entre Países Bajos-Alemania se disputará a las 20:45 horario peninsular en el Johan Cruyff Arena de Ámsterdam. El duelo se podrá ver en televisión en DAZN y en abierto en TVE y en su plataforma, RTVE Play.

articles.title: El Atlético sigue con seis... a la espera de Barrios
articles.standfirst: Canteranos del C y de Juvenil completan la sesión mientras el jugador bandera continúa dando pasos hacia su recuperación
articles.summary: Canteranos del C y de Juvenil completan la sesión mientras el jugador bandera continúa dando pasos hacia su recuperación
articles.body: Koke, Llorente, Cardoso, Le Normand, Arnau Ortiz y Dani Martínez, acompañados de más de una decena de integrantes del Atlético C y el Juvenil A, continúan siendo la representación del primer equipo en las sesiones 'en familia' que dirige Simeone durante este parón liguero. Sin embargo, las 'plegarias' y las miradas se dirigen hacia el campo anexo, a ver si asoma Barrios. De hecho, más allá de mantener el tono competitivo de los seis futbolistas a disposición del Cholo y de cruzar los dedos para que los 16 internacionales repartidos por el mundo vuelvan sanos del periplo con sus respectivas selecciones, el principal objetivo del Atlético en estas tres semanas pasa por recuperar a su jugador franquicia. Eso sí, sin prisa y con cautela. De ahí que si bien se celebra cada aparición en solitario de Barrios por el verde, también se respetan los tiempos para que su reincorporación al grupo se produzca sin riesgos y en las mejores condiciones. Así, aunque continúa dando pasos hacia la salida de la enfermería, aún permanecerá varios días más trabajando junto a los recuperadores. Del mismo modo, tampoco la vuelta de Sorloth, aún inédito esta temporada, se antoja próxima. El noruego, lesionado desde la primera semana tras el fin de sus vacaciones post Mundial, lleva un proceso más lento, sin que se atisbe de momento una fecha para que de una vez por todas pueda sumarse al grupo.

articles.title: Brentwood Town: How former Leyton Orient owner Barry Hearn is helping shape the future of his local non-league club
articles.summary: Sports promoter Barry Hearn owned Leyton Orient between 1995 and 2014; in the summer of 2026, his company Matchroom signed a five-year partnership with seventh-tier club Brentwood Town - and here, chairman Jez Dickinson explains just how that works
articles.body:
Even at 78, the Matchroom founder remains one of the world's most recognisable sporting promoters.

His involvement in football is perhaps lesser known - but every bit as intriguing.

In March 1995, Hearn saved Leyton Orient - who he first watched at the age of 11 - from bankruptcy by buying the club for just £2.43.

By 2007, three sides of Brisbane Road had been rebuilt. By 2012, he had wiped out any debt and reportedly invested around £8m.

In 2013/14, Orient reached the League One play-off final and had a rare chance to reach the second tier - but they lost 4-3 on penalties to Rotherham at Wembley. Within two months he had sold the club to Italian businessman Francesco Becchetti.

For nine years, Hearn was away from football. There was no shortage of work for him to be getting on with elsewhere.

Then, in July 2023, Matchroom sponsored the home shirt of Brentwood Town, the Isthmian League North Division side based three miles up the road from their headquarters.

The following year, Hearn took a minority stake in the club - and earlier this summer, a five-year partnership and "a significant investment" was announced.

"The reason Barry came over initially was we were doing something for Saint Francis Hospice, which he is a patron of, and he sat next to me for a game," says chairman Jez Dickinson.

"It was an entertaining game and Barry said afterwards, 'I'm never going to sit next to you again, Jez! Every time the ball went into the box, you were going up for a header and elbowing me in the side!' Barry is very much about passion and wearing his heart on his sleeve, so that's probably where we connected.

"We had some lunches and, after about the third one, he asked me what I wanted. I said obviously I wanted him to get involved, but I wanted him to get involved because he wanted to get involved, not because I was asking him - and he said he'd do it."

Hearn's name is, naturally, the one that catches the eye, but Dickinson has been the driving force since taking over as chairman in May 2019.

Before his appointment, he says there was "no pathway for the youth into the first team", "the bar was like a 1970s pub", and "the ambition was just to stay in the league".

They installed a brand new 3G pitch in the summer of 2024, won the Isthmian North Division in 2024/25 and last season lost the play-off final, where a place in the National League South was on the line.

Brentwood now have a Centre of Excellence, with 250 boys and girls between the ages of six to 12 in it. "It's hollow if that isn't there," he says.

Dickinson has spent seven years building the foundations so far - and Hearn's involvement provides the chance to take the club to another level.

"I speak to him probably once a week, maybe twice. It depends what's happening," says Dickinson.

"He's hands-on in as much as he's available for anything we talk about. We'll sit down every couple of months, look at the financials, how we're getting on. He loves his numbers!

"Though he's a minority shareholder and he owns some of the club, he doesn't want to run it. He says: 'I look at you, Jez and you're stressed enough, I don't want any of that!'

"What he does is actually raise the bar, subconsciously, for what I want to achieve. We'll have a catch-up at Matchroom and it is quite inspiring and you come away thinking, 'let's go for it'.

"I don't underestimate that. It's probably 10 times as important as the financial stuff he does - not that I don't want the financial support as that's really important!

"He's a fantastic ambassador for the club as well as a sponsor and partner. I was speaking to a potential partner recently and they said they were interested because if he's committing to five years, he doesn't do things by halves and won't give up easily. It creates confidence with us and people looking to be partners."

Dickinson says Brentwood - who sit 18th in the Isthmian Premier Division after eight games - are currently averaging attendances of just under 700, with aims of reaching 1,000 this season.

There are plans for a 1,000-seater stand in place, but their purchase of the Brentwood Centre Arena needs to be completed before any progression can be made on that front.

Where does Dickinson think the partnership with Hearn and Matchroom will take Brentwood over these next five years?

"Barry decided on a five-year partnership to drive the club to the highest level of the pyramid possible. Hopefully after those five years, there'll be another five years!

"Realistically, if we're playing National League football in five years, that will be pretty successful for us. That would be excellent.

"It shows how much faith he and Matchroom have in us - it's down to us to deliver."

articles.title: Santi Denia reemplaza a siete lesionados en la convocatoria de la República Checa
articles.standfirst: Para los encuentros que disputarán en la Nations League
articles.summary: Para los encuentros que disputarán en la Nations League
articles.body: El técnico de la selección checa de fútbol, Santi Denia, ha convocado a siete nuevos jugadores para reemplazar a los lesionados de la lista oficial de la Nations League, que arranca este sábado para los centroeuropeos con un duelo frente a la Croacia de Luka Modric, informó este jueves el diario Sport. El último de los lesionados ha sido el lateral izquierdo Matej Rynes, del Sparta Praga, en cuyo lugar fue convocado Ondrej Zmrzly, del Gornik Zabrze, que lidera la liga polaca. Al inicio de la concentración, este lunes en Praga, el técnico albacetense tuvo que rehacer los planes, ante la baja de otros seis jugadores, cinco de ellos del Slavia Praga -David Zima, David Jurasek, Tomas Vlcek, Lukas Provod y Tomas Chory-, además del medio ofensivo del Pilsen Denis Visinky. Han sido sustituidos en la lista por los defensas Martin Vitik (Bolonia), Vaclav Sejka, Ondrej Kricfalusi (Union Saint-Gilloise) y Jiri Slama, así como el centrocampista Martin Subert, actual máximo goleador de la liga checa, y el delantero centro Daniel Vasulin. Krickfalusi, Subert, Slama y Vasulin debutan en la selección absoluta, una apuesta por nuevos talentos en un colectivo del que Denia asumió las riendas a finales de julio, en sustitución de Miroslav Koubek, que dirigió a los checos durante el Mundial, donde no lograron pasar de la fase de grupos.

articles.title: Última sesión del Barça sobre el césped: mañana, gimnasio y... vacaciones
articles.standfirst: Flick recurre hoy a cuatro jugadores del filial
articles.summary: Flick recurre hoy a cuatro jugadores del filial
articles.body: El Barcelona trabajó esta mañana en la Ciudad Deportiva, y lo volvió a hacer en familia. El equipo culé tiene a 17 jugadores repartidos con sus respectivas selecciones y a cuatro lesionados, por lo que Flick sólo dispone de seis profesionales del primer equipo. El técnico alemán amplió el quórum de la sesión, la última sobre el césped de esta semana y durante muchos días, con cuatro canteranos. Hansi Flick dirigió hoy el entrenamiento en la Ciudad Deportiva con muy pocos efectivos, como está siendo habitual estos días a causa de los compromisos internacionales. El preparador germano trabajó con Balde, Brian Fariñas, Gavi, Gabriel Jesus, Tek y Gerard Martín, así como Eder Aller, Hafiz, Guillem Víctor y Shane Kluivert, del Barça Atlètic. Fue la última sesión del Barça de la semana sobre el césped, ya que mañana viernes el entrenamiento está programado para que sea sólo en el gimnasio. Tras este trabajo, los azulgranas disfrutarán de nueve días de descanso, ya que Flick no los ha citado de nuevo hasta el lunes 5 de octubre. De todas formas, a priori, los cuatro jugadores que están lesionados sí que se pasarán por las instalaciones del Barcelona para seguir con la recuperación de sus respectivas molestias. Están en la enfermería: Frenkie de Jong, Joan García, Christensen y Roony.

articles.title: Expert CFB Locks for Florida vs. Ole Miss and Week 4's Biggest Games
articles.summary: Some weeks, the losses just wash off of you. You make a pick; it wins or loses, and you move forward. More times than not, that's what the weekly ritual looks like.
articles.body:
Some weeks, the losses just wash off of you. You make a pick; it wins or loses, and you move forward. More times than not, that's what the weekly ritual looks like.

Some losses sit with you for much longer. In certain weeks, these moments—or "bad beats"—somehow pile up, making you wonder if the Football Gods are working against you.

We were on North Carolina State last week. The Wolfpack lost in historic fashion on the freakiest of final-second moments. If you haven't seen it yet, you can do so here . I've seen it enough.

We had North Carolina, too. The Tar Heels were up comfortably and driving before a weather delay stalled the momentum. Clemson then scored a touchdown late on a broken run to push this one the other way.

We could dwell on it a while longer, or we could move on. This sport is too glorious to bask in these bad beats for long. Instead, let's turn these moments into consistent winners.

It's hard to imagine a football game this season with greater hangover potential than this one. To be honest, for Ole Miss, it's completely and utterly understandable.

All that emotion that went into last week's win over LSU—especially over former head coach Lane Kiffin—will unquestionably linger. Given all the hoopla, how could it not?

Heading to Florida to take on a dangerous program and a rejuvenated fan base in a difficult environment is a less-than-ideal encore after the weekend.

Granted, they still have Trinidad Chambliss. The Rebels' exceptional quarterback can make the impossible possible. He'll certainly test a Florida defense that just allowed 39 points.

Perhaps more concerning for the Gators, however, are the penalties. Last week, they tallied 16 in total for 138 yards. That won't fly against a quarterback and team this good. Period.

On the flip side, Florida has weapons. The wideouts are electric and running back Jadan Baugh might be the best player at his position in the whole country. The quarterback mismatch in this game might look robust, although Aaron Philo has been solid so far.

The talent is there, but sometimes games are decided by more than just players. Ole Miss, coming off one of its biggest wins in program history, will hit the road for the very first time.

The Gators are in prime position to take full advantage.

One of these two teams is about to begin the season 0-2 in conference play.

Given the resources dumped into the roster, that reality is likely unacceptable to each fan base. And while desperation isn't necessarily an angle, it could provide both teams with plenty of motivation.

Presently, neither offense ranks in the top 35. Right now, neither offense feels stable, with injuries playing a role in that, too.

Still, both sides have speed and big-play potential.

Texas A&M was lucky to get past Arizona State a few weeks ago. The defense allowed nearly 400 yards of offense in that win, as the signs were there. A week later, Kentucky totaled 408 yards of offense in an upset win.

As for the quarterbacks, both are intriguing. Sam Leavitt and Marcel Reed produce in different ways, but the volatility of their performances could both help or hurt. Both score touchdowns. Both turn the ball over.

In this instance, the good—and the very bad—could help produce points. That's what we're in search of. That's what we'll get.

Through three games, Utah has outscored its opponents by a combined score of 142 to 24.

This includes a dominant win over Arkansas and a 33-0 shutout of Utah State in Week 3. What the Utes have yet to do, however, is play a football game on the road.

A trip to Ames, Iowa, a campus that has played spoiler—or at the very least flirted with the concept—will be a telling next step for a Utah team still growing comfortable with a new head coach.

So far, so good for Morgan Scalley, although moments like these will be telling.

As for Iowa State, I owe this team an apology. Given the mass exodus that took place when former head coach Matt Campbell left for Penn State, this season looked to be lost on paper. To date, however, the Cyclones have played hard.

This defense has been excellent, quarterback Jaylen Raynor has been solid and the results so far have been encouraging. Iowa State's 16-13 loss to rival Iowa on the road was eye-opening. Playing at home against a team that has yet to play outside its own stadium should be an advantage.

Ultimately, Utah wins, but Iowa State keeps it tight.

Ranking the Most NFL Pro-Ready College Football Athletes 🔢

One team has been tested. The other really hasn't.

While one could easily declare Texas' rousing comeback against Ohio State the deciding factor in a game of this magnitude, this feels more complicated. The last 15 minutes of that game against the Buckeyes was indeed impressive. The first 30 minutes, however, were a bit of a mess.

For Texas, are we ready to fully trust Arch Manning in this offense at one of the best venues in college football? Maybe we should be, although this game (and spread) implies a challenge is in store.

In the early part of the season, the Vols have a few things working, albeit against manageable opponents.

Tennessee is currently No. 3 in sacks and No. 4 in rushing offense. Putting Manning in uncomfortable situations with pressure is a vital part of the game plan. Working the clock and running the ball is another. Such is an ideal formula to beat good teams.

While the Longhorns have the more talented roster, Tennessee is doing a lot of very important things well early on. Those things will be tested this weekend, although a competitive game seems likely.

The other side of last week's NC State shocker, of course, was a Vanderbilt victory.

Indeed, the Commodores were gift-wrapped a victory in epic fashion, although there will be no time to bask in the afterglow. A trip to Auburn is on tap, which is still an extremely difficult place to play, even if Florida made it look somewhat easy at times.

The good news for the Tigers is that they totaled nearly 400 yards of offense. The bad news? They allowed nearly 500.

The Auburn passing game finally showed some life. The flashes from QB Byrum Brown were there. After scoring just 17 points against Baylor in Week 1, the offense did a lot of really solid things, as the talent is evident.

For Vanderbilt, this will mark Jared Curtis' first road game. The 5-star true freshman throws a gorgeous football. Last game, however, he threw the ball twice to the other team.

At just 19 years old, this feels like a tall ask. Although Vanderbilt is 3-0, the performances haven't been dazzling. The point spread speaks to that, in many respects.

Auburn has by no means been perfect, but this feels like a matchup that could get potentially lopsided.

Simply put, Georgia Tech isn't the same team it was a season ago. In fact, the Yellow Jackets are nowhere close. While Stanford is a massive work in progress, this game feels very much up for grabs.

We're back on the Maryland bandwagon, perhaps so a little reluctantly. The Terps were unable to keep up with Virginia Tech last week, but UCLA's long road trip makes this one an interesting spot. Mike Locksley needs this one.

UTSA's game against Texas last week went as one might expect. That doesn't mean this team isn't capable. In fact, the win over Texas State in Week 2 looks good now. At home, this scoreboard could get sideways.

articles.title: Latest College Football Odds and Picks Factoring in New Weather Forecasts for Week 4 Schedule
articles.summary: Week 4 has the feel of the first of many make-or-break weekend for a handful of College Football Playoff contenders.
articles.body:
Week 4 has the feel of the first of many make-or-break weekend for a handful of College Football Playoff contenders.

Six games takes place on Saturday between AP Top 25 teams.

Arch Manning and the top-ranked Texas Longhorns open the day with an early-afternoon trip to visit the Tennessee Volunteers.

That SEC clash doesn't have nearly as much drama as the primetime clash in Baton Rouge between the Texas A&M Aggies and LSU Tigers does. That matchup has the feel of a potential playoff elimination game.

Dante Moore and the Oregon Ducks might be in a similar situation on the road against the USC Trojans.

A&M, LSU and Oregon all enter the weekend with one loss. A second loss before the start of October might be too much to overcome to qualify for the 12-team playoff.

All of the forecasts and key weather information for Saturday's games can be found here on The Weather Channel.

Week 4 Top 25 Schedule, Odds and Weather

Sam Houston at No. 11 Texas Tech (-34.5)

Prediction: Texas Tech 44, Sam Houston 17

Wake Forest at No. 16 Louisville (-13.5)

Prediction: Louisville 31, Wake Forest 21

No. 25 Houston (-18.5) at Georgia Southern

Prediction: Houston 31, Georgia Southern 17

Prediction: Miami 55, Central Michigan 10

Prediction: Alabama 37, South Carolina 17

No. 19 Missouri at No. 24 Mississippi State (-6.5)

Prediction: Missouri 27, Mississippi State 23

Arch Manning, Cam Coleman and the Texas Longhorns go on the road for the first time this season on Saturday in Knoxville.

They'll have ideal conditions to play in at Neyland Stadium. The high is projected to be 78 degrees in Knoxville on Saturday.

The Tennessee Volunteers haven't made much national noise yet in 2026 because they've produced three blowout wins.

Week 4 is the first chance for Josh Heupel's team to impress against a big-time opponent.

It'll also serve as the first test of freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon, who threw for 552 yards and six touchdowns in the opening three games.

Texas owns the advantage in experience across the board on offense, but that unit does come into Saturday with something to prove.

Manning had an up-and-down campaign away from home in 2025. He lost two games, completed under 65 percent of his passes in three of four road contests and threw two picks in a game in a road loss to the Florida Gators.

The nephew of Tennessee great Peyton Manning needs to play better on the road in 2026 for the Longhorns to retain their top ranking.

While the game is in Tennessee, the focus is solely on Texas and how its big-name players perform on the road.

Manning showcased that he could deliver in the clutch in Week 2 against the Ohio State Buckeyes. If he's better in the first three quarters on Saturday than he was in Week 2, we could walk away from the game with a better impression of the Texas quarterback.

The premier SEC primetime clash of the weekend feels like a defacto CFB Playoff elimination game.

The Texas A&M Aggies and LSU Tigers are both coming off losses to kick off their respective SEC schedules.

Two losses in the SEC, where the schedules don't get any easier as the season goes on, before October 1 feels like a death sentence for a team's playoff viability.

LSU is an 8.5-point favorite because of its home-field advantage in Baton Rouge and its play from the first two weeks.

However, you'd be right to be hesitant about backing the Tigers off a loss to the Ole Miss Rebels and in a game without one of their star pass-catchers in Trey'Dez Green.

Green is one of the best tight ends and red-zone targets in the country. Sam Leavitt needs to open up the passing game more to suit his wide receivers, starting with Jayce Brown and Winston Watkins Jr.

The good news for LSU's offense is that it faces an A&M defense that gave up 408 total yards at home in the Week 3 loss to the Kentucky Wildcats.

Marcel Reed also struggled in the pocket in that defeat with two interceptions. The A&M quarterback threw multiple interceptions four times last season. All of those occurrences were against Top 25 foes.

Reed feasted on weaker teams last season, but he didn't fully meet the challenge of big games, especially at the end of the year versus Texas and the Miami Hurricanes.

Reed's turnover issues are a big red flag for A&M, which makes it more difficult to bet A&M as a touchdown-plus underdog than it does LSU as a strong favorite at home.

No one expected the Oregon Ducks' playoff hopes to be near life support by the end of September.

That's the reality with Dante Moore and Co. as they head to Los Angeles on Saturday night to face the USC Trojans.

Oregon's stunning road loss to the Oklahoma State Cowboys in Week 2 put it in a perilous spot in the playoff conversation. USC is the first of three Top 25 opponents the Ducks face in Big Ten play.

Moore and Co. bounced back in resounding fashion in Week 3 with an 84-0 win over the FCS Portland State Vikings.

Moore hasn't turned the ball over through the air yet this season, but he did only complete 48.5 percent of his passes against OK State.

USC's Jayden Maiava owns a 75.7 completion percentage, 1,173 yards, 12 touchdowns and a single INT through four games.

USC scored at least 39 points in each of its four victories. It likely needs to hit the 35-40-mark again in Week 4 because its defense has struggled.

The Trojans conceded at least 26 points in three of their four games and are coming off a 42-35 win over the Rutgers Scarlet Knights, who are widely viewed as one of the worst teams in the Big Ten.

At minimum, points are expected at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The over/under of 62.5 might be too low if the two quarterbacks find a rhythm early.

articles.title: Hibs appoint Dutchman Reedijk as new manager
articles.summary: Former Beveren head coach Marink Reedijk vows to develop a "brave, intense and committed" Hibernian team after becoming the club's new manager.
articles.body:
Former Beveren head coach Marink Reedijk has vowed to develop a "brave, intense and committed" Hibernian team after becoming the club's new manager.

The Dutchman, 35, replaces David Gray, who was sacked eight days ago after a difficult start to the term for the Scottish Premiership outfit.

Reedijk has spent the last two seasons with Beveren, earning promotion to the top flight last season after an unbeaten campaign before leaving in the summer.

He previous worked in academy roles at Ajax and West Bromwich Albion, and in with the senior teams at KSV Roeselare, Vitesse and RSCA Futures.

Hibs say Reedijk - who is "honoured" to be appointed - arrives with a reputation for attacking football and building a strong team culture.

"I can feel the ambition and see the clarity of what the club is trying to achieve," he said. "That was a big part of what attracted me here.

"I want us to be an assertive team. A team that gives everything, plays with purpose and gives our supporters something to really get behind."

Latest Hibs news, analysis and fan views

Get Hibs news notifications in the BBC Sport app

Reedijk will be assisted by Rogier Molhoek at Easter Road, with the club hailing his arrival as "an exciting moment".

The Edinburgh outfit are currently 10th in the Premiership, with two wins from their opening seven matches, and endured a gut-wrenching Conference League exit.

Under Gray, they finished third in 2024/25 and fifth last term, with the departed manager also leading them to November's League Cup semi-finals, where they will face city rivals Hearts.

Sporting director Malky Mackay insists Reedijk's recruitment is not about "changing the direction" of their footbal strategy, but is about "continuing to evolve it".

"We believe Marink is an excellent fit to take the team forward," he added.

"We began this process with a clear idea of the type of team we want to continue to build and the qualities we wanted from our next manager. Marink's philosophy, his work with players and his leadership style are strongly aligned with that.

"His teams are proactive, high energy and dynamic. What also stands out is his ability to develop individuals and create a strong collective environment."

Ross: Decent appointment, time will tell if it's the right one. His credentials and philosophy sits well with me and what we want to achieve. Welcome and all the best.

Lee: Another young manager! Let's get behind him, and the team and give him a chance to show what he is capable of. I hope it works out, because if it doesn't, beyond the dugout is where the spotlight should be.

Tony: Brilliant, good to have someone in quickly. Not a great knowledge of the guy but from what I've read he likes an attacking team with wingers so that's a positive. Will be good to see what he can do with the current squad. It probably won't solve it quickly but let's see.
