articles.title: Dani Calvo, capitán del Oviedo: "En el derbi vamos a salir a matar"
articles.standfirst: "Es una final para la afición y para nosotros. Los nuevos ya saben lo importante que es conseguir los tres puntos", ha asegurado
articles.summary: "Es una final para la afición y para nosotros. Los nuevos ya saben lo importante que es conseguir los tres puntos", ha asegurado
articles.body: El derbi asturiano se disputará este domingo entre el Real Oviedo y el Real Sporting (Carlos Tartiere, 21.00 horas) y el capital azul, Dani Calvo, aseguró que su equipo "saldrá a matar". "Le estamos dando la relevancia que tiene este partido. Aunque sólo sean tres puntos, está marcado en el calendario para todos. Es una final para la afición y para nosotros. Los nuevos ya saben lo importante que es conseguir los tres puntos", explicó el central en la sala de prensa de El Requexón. La plantilla del Real Oviedo sólo cuenta con tres asturianos y canteranos, todos con ficha del filial, aunque Calvo considera que "el devenir del encuentro no se verá afectado por dicho aspecto", aunque reconoció que cuando había más canteranos en plantilla "esos jugadores eran los más intensos durante la semana". "La figura de Santi Cazorla la echo de menos siempre, asturiano y oviedista, representa al Oviedo en su sangre. Su figura siempre es importante, nos servía a los compañeros para apoyarnos en él", afirmó el defensa oscense al ser preguntado por Cazorla, que se retiró este verano. El Real Oviedo completó esta mañana el antepenúltimo entrenamiento antes de recibir el domingo al Sporting, partido que no podrá jugar el extremo azul Estanis Pedrola, que sufre una luxación en el hombro izquierdo y, aunque no pasará por el quirófano, se perderá varios encuentros de liga

articles.title: Diallo, talismán para el Granada
articles.standfirst: Los rojiblancos no han logrado ganar ninguno de los partidos en los que el francés ha estado fuera del terreno de juego
articles.summary: Los rojiblancos no han logrado ganar ninguno de los partidos en los que el francés ha estado fuera del terreno de juego
articles.body: Procedente de la segunda división francesa, Diallo desembarcó en el Granada sin hacer ruido, fuera del radar, pero pronto se convirtió en pieza indispensable para Pacheta, una importancia que se pone de manifiesto con sus ausencias, un escenario sin el galo sobre el terreno de juego en el que el Granada ha sido incapaz de ganar. Desde su llegada a Los Cármenes el curso pasado, Diallo se ha perdido 11 encuentros, con un saldo para el conjunto andaluz de nueve derrotas y dos empates, cifras elocuentes que hablan de la importancia del galo en el engranaje rojiblanco, que se resiente cuando el defensor no puede estar junto a sus compañeros en el verde. Este curso, el Granada arrancó con fuerza, sumando un empate y dos victorias para comenzar, pero tras el triunfo en El Arcángel Diallo se lesionó el tobillo durante un entrenamiento, teniendo que parar. En las siguientes tres jornadas, con el galo en el dique seco, los nazaríes han encajado dos derrotas y solo han sumado un punto, un cambio de tendencia pronunciado que coincide con la ausencia del lateral. Esta ‘Diallo dependencia’ ya la sufrió el equipo en la anterior campaña, cuando el de Toulouse también tuvo problemas físicos en el inicio de la competición, perdiéndose cuatro encuentros en los que los rojiblancos fueron incapaces de ganar, algo que se repitió en los otros cuatros choques más que se perdió el zurdo a lo largo de la campaña. Ahora, concentrado con Mauritania cuando aún no había recibido el alta competitiva, Diallo tampoco estará ayudando al equipo contra el Andorra, una oportunidad para que los de Pacheta rompan esta especie de maldición y aprendan a ganar sin Diallo.

articles.title: Bisiwu: "El jugador que más me ha impresionado es Raphinha"
articles.standfirst: El joven jugador destaca la calidad técnica de Pedri y Lamine Yamal
articles.summary: El joven jugador destaca la calidad técnica de Pedri y Lamine Yamal
articles.body: Bisiwu no escatima en elogios hacia Raphinha. El joven delantero, que llegó este verano al Barcelona procedente del Brujas, se encuentra actualmente concentrado con la selección sub-21 de Bélgica y desde allí explicó que el brasileño es un ejemplo por su actitud tanto en los entrenamientos como en los partidos. “El futbolista que más me ha sorprendido es Raphinha. Siempre juega y se entrena al cien por cien. Estoy impresionado. Es un modelo para mí”, explicó el delantero en declaraciones a RTL. Bisiwu tuvo la oportunidad de trabajar junto al primer equipo durante la pretemporada nada más aterrizar en Barcelona. Sin embargo, por el momento no está disfrutando de oportunidades a las órdenes de Flick y sus minutos como culé están siendo con filial. Más allá de Raphinha, el delantero también puso el foco en otros dos futbolistas del Barça a los que considera especialmente destacados desde el punto de vista táctico. En este caso, se decantó por Lamine Yamal y Pedri. El azulgrana también valoró sus primeras semanas en el Barça y aseguró que su adaptación a la entidad está siendo muy positiva. Bisiwu se mostró agradecido por la acogida que recibió desde su llegada. “Ha ido todo muy bien, me han acogido muy bien. He podido hablar con el capitán y con el entrenador y me he sentido muy bien”, reconoció. Su fichaje por el Barcelona ha tenido consecuencias en su papel dentro de la selección sub-21 de Bélgica. Bisiwu es consciente de que ahora existe una mayor atención mediática sobre su figura y reconoce que su llegada al club azulgrana ha supuesto un cambio en su estatus. “Sí, siento un cambio de estatus porque llegar al Barça, fichar por el Barça, no es un asunto menor y he podido sentir ese impacto. Ahora estoy centrado en la sub-21”, señaló.

articles.title: Convocados de España para el Mundial de pádel 2026: Aimar Goñi, la gran novedad de Juanjo Gutiérrez
articles.standfirst: El navarro de 20 años se 'cuela' en la lista de 8 integrantes para la cita definitiva en Doha del 2 al 7 de noviembre
articles.summary: El navarro de 20 años se 'cuela' en la lista de 8 integrantes para la cita definitiva en Doha del 2 al 7 de noviembre
articles.body: La selección española de pádel ha hecho oficial hoy la convocatoria para el Mundial 2026 que se disputará del 2 al 7 de noviembre en Doha (Qatar) y donde el combinado de Juanjo Gutiérrez buscará su quinto Mundial masculino de la historia. El seleccionador ha hecho pública hoy la lista en Madrid en un acto celebrado en el CUPRA City Garage de la Calle Serrano donde se han anunciado los representantes nacionales que buscarán la gloria cinco años después del último título, conquistado precisamente en la capital qatarí. La gran novedad de la convocatoria ha sido Aimar Goñi, el navarro de 20 años quien, como adelantó MARCA hace tres meses, era uno de los grandes 'tapados' de Juanjo Gutiérrez para la cita mundialista. El único debutante de esta terna de elegidos es actualmente pareja 10 con Edu Alonso y número 32 del ránking FIP. Goñi acompañará a los otros tres jugadores de revés 'fijos' para el seleccionador: Alejandro Galán, Paquito Navarro y Coki Nieto. Los tres levantaron el título Mundial hace cinco años en el Khalifa Complex de Doha y estuvieron también en las dos ediciones posteriores que se llevó Argentina. La lista la completan, de jugadores de derecha, los siguientes: Arturo Coello, Juan Lebrón, Mike Yanguas y Jon Sanz. Este último era otra de las grandes dudas de la convocatoria, pero finalmente se ha hecho un hueco dejando atrás a los preseleccionados Fran Guerrero y Pol Hernández. -Alejandro Galán -Paquito Navarro -Coki Nieto -Aimar Goñi -Arturo Coello -Juan Lebrón -Mike Yanguas -Jon Sanz

articles.title: From ruin to a (Red) Bull market - how Prem became hot property
articles.summary: Prem Rugby seemed on the brink of disaster after Worcester, Wasps and London Irish went bust, but there is renewed confidence and fresh money in the league.
articles.body:
Simon Massie-Taylor pulled up outside Newcastle's Kingston Park stadium, and saw fear.

The unannounced arrival of Prem Rugby's chief executive at one of the league's clubs had rarely been a good sign.

Massie-Taylor started the role in January 2022. In the 18 months that followed, Wasps, Worcester and London Irish, with finances stretched out of shape by Covid, had flamed out of the English top flight.

"When those clubs were going into administration, the common denominator was their leadership leaving the room," remembers Massie-Taylor.

"The owners, the chief executives, everyone went.

"So it was basically up to me, [Rugby Players Association general secretary] Christian Day and [Rugby Football Union director of legal and governance] Angus Bujalski to go in and say, 'we're terribly sorry, this is what's happened, this is what it means for you'.

"Telling anyone that they've lost their job is one of the worst bits of having a job. But when it comes to sport, for the people that work in those clubs, it's not just a job, it's a way of life. It was horrible."

So when Massie-Taylor pitched up at Newcastle last year, with the club limping from payroll to payroll, onlookers feared the worse.

"Some of the players and staff, when they first saw me, thought I was this grim reaper figure coming to deliver another bad news story," he said.

Instead he ushered Newcastle's staff into a room decked out in the blue and silver branding of Red Bull.

Backed by a hype video filled with signature extreme sport stunts, executives from the energy drink giant, fresh off a flight, spelled out a grand vision for the Prem's bottom club.

"There were people in that room in tears, it was pretty special," said Massie-Taylor.

That investment was a pivot point for the league.

Massie-Taylor remembers how low the bar was to buy into the Prem in his first few, stressful years. "It was 'do you exist, have you got a criminal record, do you actually have any money?," he says.

But Red Bull's arrival, sealed and delivered in August 2025, marked a sea change.

Since then Black Knight - the owners of Premier League side Bournemouth - have bought up Exeter Chiefs, billionaire industrialist Sir James Dyson has taken a 50% share of Bath and financier Steve Zander has made a multi-million pound investment into Northampton Saints.

More outside investment is expected soon, with Gloucester and Leicester among those in conversations.

"Investor interest in the league has increased significantly in the last 12 months, certainly the last six," says Massie-Taylor, who convened a summit for prospective buyers in London in June and is heading to the United States in October to press flesh and make the case.

His confidence is shared by more impartial experts.

Matthew Wheeler helped broker Red Bull's takeover of Newcastle, but his specialist investment group A&W Capital has made deals across a variety of sports and media.

"I don't think you're drunk from the Kool-Aid to have belief in the Prem, there definitely is a momentum behind it," he says.

Andrew Umbers is a co-founder of Oakwell Sports Advisory, which had a similar role in Exeter's takeover.

"We put Exeter in front just over 110 sports investors and we had interest probably from around 30," he says. "That interest came from North America, Asia and continental Europe."

It is quite the difference from when Massie-Taylor would entertain enquiries from anyone with proof of identity, a clean chargesheet and a positive bank balance.

There are a few factors that are happy coincidence, rather than canny design.

The value of sports teams generally has risen steeply. The sale of the LA Lakers for a record $12.5bn (£9.3bn) this summer is the prime example.

Wheeler puts the spike down to the guaranteed eyeballs sport attracts in a fragmented media world, its relative resistance to disruption by artificial intelligence as a product and the prestige and scarcity value of owning a sports team.

Prem Rugby was also on an upward growth trajectory before the Covid pandemic hit. Even with the loss of three teams, a return to normality has allowed the league to rediscover that groove.

A brand of the heft of Red Bull getting involved in the league, undoubtedly sparked interest elsewhere.

However, proactive changes have played a part.

An independent financial monitoring panel has kept across all Prem club finances for the past couple of seasons, and is designed to prevent dangerous levels of risk and spending. That has reassured investors.

With a funding deal with the Rugby Football Union and broadcast partnership with TNT Sports locked in for several seasons, there is stability for the foreseeable.

A calendar shift has meant England internationals are available more often to their clubs, raising the wattage on the domestic game's star power.

And, while Massie-Taylor won't say it himself, he has inspired confidence. A former investment banker, he understands what prospective buyers are looking for.

"The governance is important because the first thing an investor wants to know is can they rely on the management and is the league going to be well run.

"You may be buying into an individual team, but you're really buying into the league.

"You can have the most successful team you want, but if the league's not successful, it doesn't mean anything."

Massie-Taylor's most important decision might be his most controversial.

He backed the ring-fencing of the league, scrapping relegation and bringing new teams in via a tender process rather than achievements on the pitch.

This season is the first to be played out without even a hint of jeopardy at the bottom of the table.

While some see a betrayal of sporting tradition, the change gives Prem Rugby a point of difference over lower-level football sides competing for the same investment.

No possible drop down the leagues, no danger of a distressed asset.

"It is a real thing for US investors," says Massie-Taylor.

"There was a fear and, to some extent, a handbrake on investment because of that financial jeopardy."

It is just one aspect of the league that makes prospective American buyers comfortable.

The upper and, from this season, lower limits on how much Prem clubs can spend on players' salaries are common in Stateside sport, as is the equitable sharing of media revenues.

There has also been a shift to centralise deals and maximise revenues.

A proposal to have one kit manufacturer for the whole league - something seen in America's 'big four' leagues (NBA, NFL, MLB and NHL) - has been floated in the past.

"For an investor, owning a Prem Rugby team is more is more like owning an NFL team than it is like owning a Premier League football team [in that regard]," says Wheeler.

It was noticeable that Brett Gosper, formerly the head of World Rugby, now leading NFL Europe, was on hand at Prem Rugby's investor summit to underline those parallels.

The combination of features of a franchise league, with the long rivalries and established, loyal fanbases that a start-up competition lacks, makes the Prem a rare prospect.

"American investors are interested in under-commercialised sport, below the tier-one leagues such as Premier League, NFL or the IPL, that are at a turning point in their cycle," says Umbers.

"Rugby is not a big sport in America, so there has got to be some education going on," he says.

"But will American investors be interested once they understand the dynamics? Yes."

Massie-Taylor knows the margins are narrow.

A 10-team league cannot afford any more clubs to go under. There are financial debts and a dependency on owner generosity across the league.

"We've proved there's opportunity going forward," he says.

"The thing that's niggling us now is the fear that we don't make the most of it. That's the pressure we all feel to really crack on."

It isn't just the players aiming to start the season fast.
authors: Mike Henson - BBC Sport rugby union news reporter

articles.title: Arsenal: USA international Emily Fox signs new deal with Women's Super League club
articles.summary: Emily Fox joined Arsenal from North Carolina Courage in January 2024 and is closing in on 100 appearances for the club; in an exclusive interview with Sky Sports the 28-year-old said it was "a very easy decision to want to stay"
articles.body:
The 28-year-old joined the Gunners from North Carolina Courage in January 2024 and has made 93 appearances, scoring three goals.

She was nominated for the Ballon d'Or in 2025.

Speaking in an exclusive interview with Sky Sports , USA international Fox said: "It was easy - I love the club.

"I'm being challenged in a competitive environment and it's my second home. A very easy decision to want to stay.

"I've got a mindset to get better and more to prove. I'm always hungry as a player and leaning towards perfection. When I'm playing with the best players in the world, there are so many things I can learn.

"I want to push myself and in an environment where I'm challenged, there's consistency every day and matching it. I want to be even more consistent to prove myself."

Fox the perfect blend of modern and old-school full-back

Tying Emily Fox down to a new contract was something Arsenal have been wanting to do for a while. It's easy to see why. The American has been one of the most consistent full-backs in the league since joining in 2024.

She is a modern-day full-back, but in the most traditional sense. By that I mean she runs the channels with intelligence, a constant source of energy and offensive threat, but does not shirk her defensive duties. The picture of reliability in both directions.

What I is especially like is how progressive she is in possession, always looking to pass forwards and someone who rarely gives the ball away. As Arsenal attempt to establish some rhythm in the early knockings of this season, the 28-year-old is an important stabilising figure to keep around. Her consistency is something Renee Slegers can depend on.

articles.title: Hibernian appoint Marink Reedijk: Thirty-four year old Dutchman arrives at Easter Road after success in Belgium
articles.summary: Marink Reedijk appointed as successor to David Gray after leading SK Beveren to an unbeaten title-winning season in Belgium's second tier; Hibs are 10th in Scottish Premiership with two wins from seven games
articles.body:
Dutchman Reedijk arrives from SK Beveren, having won the Belgian second-tier title with an unbeaten campaign.

The 34-year-old has also worked in academy positions at Ajax and West Bromwich Albion.

Reedijk, said: "I am honoured to be appointed manager of Hibernian Football Club.

"This is one of the biggest clubs in Scottish football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand.

"I can feel the ambition and see the clarity of what the club is trying to achieve. That was a big part of what attracted me here.

"I want us to be an assertive team - brave, intense and committed. A team that gives everything, plays with purpose and gives our supporters something to really get behind.

"There is quality and potential in the squad, and good work has already been done. My first job is to get to know the players, build on those foundations and make sure we are ready for Dundee United."

Reedijk will now travel to La Manga with the team on Saturday for a training camp, with his first match a Scottish Premiership trip to Dundee United on October 10.

Hibs are currently 10th in the Scottish Premiership, with just two wins from their opening seven fixtures.

Hibernian sporting director, Malky Mackay , said: "Marink's appointment is an exciting moment for Hibernian Football Club.

"We began this process with a clear idea of the type of team we want to continue to build and the qualities we wanted from our next Manager. Marink's football philosophy, his work with players and his leadership style are strongly aligned with that.

"His teams are proactive, high energy and dynamic. What also stands out is his ability to develop individuals and create a strong collective environment.

"This is not about changing the direction of our football strategy. It is about continuing to evolve it, and we believe Marink is an excellent fit to take the team forward."

Hibernian executive chairman, Ian Gordon , said: "Marink was the standout candidate. He impressed everyone involved in the process with his clarity, intelligence and drive.

"He shares our ambition to develop players and consistently compete at the top end of Scottish football and in Europe.

"Marink has our backing, and we will continue to invest in the team to give him the best possible platform to succeed.

"We're delighted to welcome Marink and his family to the club."

images.caption: Image: New Hibernian boss Marinus Reedijk during his time in charge of SK Beveren
